text:
Maria Chen: Heads up — g2-rack2-node07 flapped with two Xid 31s during the overnight soak. I put it in quarantine but didn't start full burn-in yet.
Akash Patel: Thanks. Did ECC counters move or just transient Xids?
Maria Chen: ECC stayed low, Xid spike happened at 03:12 UTC and again at 03:18. Both logs show `volta_fault` and a PCIe reset.
Liam O'Connor: Can we run the rapid repro harness before we schedule a return? I want to avoid churning capacity.
Zoe Kim: Agreed. Proposal: run targeted rapid-repro (10m stress, memory hammer, nvml ECC probe), then 6h soak if repros seen. If nothing, 24h queue with low-impact tests.
Maria Chen: TL;DR: repro steps I used locally (quick):
```bash
# quick repro (run on node in quarantine)
sudo systemctl stop kubelet
docker run --gpus all --rm --privileged --pid=host ng-stress:latest \
  bash -lc "stress-ng --gpu 2 --timeout 600s && ./gpu-memtest --passes 3"
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.uncorrected.reserved,ecc.errors.corrected.total --format=csv
journalctl -u kernel -n 200 | grep -i xid || true
```
Akash Patel: Nice. Can we add a small canary job that runs across other nodes in the same rack to rule out rack-level power/PCIe issues?
Maria Chen: Yep — I kicked a 5-node canary with staggered start times (1m apart). No other nodes tripped.
ops-bot: [deploy-burnin] started rapid-repro job on g2-rack2-node07 by Maria Chen. Job id: burnin-2143658700-1.
Liam O'Connor: If repro is intermittent, let's collect full NVLink/PCIe telemetry: `nvidia-smi -q -d PERF,DCGM` and the kernel oops dumps. Also grab PCIe link stats from `lspci -vvv`.
Zoe Kim: Also ping hw-supplier@partners — if we see repeated Xid 31 + PCIe resets within 48h, escalate for RMA. We should attach the burn-in logs and thermal curves.
Maria Chen: Cost/time tradeoff: a full 72h soak costs ~6 GPU-days (we lose node capacity). For enterprise regions with tight SLAs we prefer quicker repro + targeted RMA. For low-risk racks we might do 24h soak.
Akash Patel: Can we automate the decision? If repro hits within 2 hours -> immediate RMA + remove from pool. If only ECC drift and no Xid -> 24h soak + monitor.
Maria Chen: I pushed a tiny update to the soak scheduler to implement that rule. Config snippet:
```yaml
soak_policy:
  repro_window_minutes: 120
  immediate_rma_on_xid: true
  extended_soak_hours_if_only_ecc: 24
```
ops-bot: [soak-scheduler] updated config by Maria Chen.
Liam O'Connor: One operational note — when draining, set `kube.DrainOptions{force=true,gracePeriod=60s}` for rapid drains, but only after marking node `unschedulable=true` so no new pods land mid-test.
Zoe Kim: Also add a telemetry tag `quarantine_source=soak-harness` so we can query Prometheus for correlated events easily.
Maria Chen: Done. I kicked burnin-2143658700-1 -> repro hit at 2143658905 (Xid 31). Collected logs and opened ticket HW-9873 with hw-supplier.
Akash Patel: Thanks — next steps: RMA approved, move node to replacement flow, and spin up an ephemeral replacement in the same AZ to keep capacity. Can someone handle the AZ capacity check?
Liam O'Connor: I'll take it. Checking spare pool now, will prefer warm spare in us-west-2a. If none, we'll redistribute jobs for next 6h and schedule hot-spot scaling.
Zoe Kim: Good. Once RMA is confirmed, annotate the node `rma:approved` and run a final smoke test on the replacement before rejoin.
Maria Chen: Will attach repro artifacts to HW-9873 and put a short runbook in the ticket: repro steps, nvml dumps, `dmesg` excerpt, thermal logs, and the soak policy decision.
Akash Patel: Thanks team. Small follow-up: let's add a short blameless postmortem template for soak-triggered RMAs so we capture cost impact and time-to-RMA.
Maria Chen: Agreed — I’ll draft and share in #postmortems. :thumbsup:
